notes.subject: car
notes.text: All coverage uses a white car with no antenna; South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini have the same car.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: White front plates and yellow rear plates, UK-style; only Namibia also mostly has yellow rears in southern Africa.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Signs are mostly in English, town names come from local languages, and the Dutch-related language is very rare.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Dry and mostly flat with shrubs, small trees and golden grass; sandy soil from white to red. Border areas next door look similar.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Yellow edge lines and white centre lines, as in the rest of southern Africa; arid yellow-edged roads elsewhere drive on the right.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Unique black-and-yellow striped signposts, more rarely red-and-white; no other southern African country has these.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Curbs and guardrails are usually striped: black-yellow, red-white or black-white.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Small red-and-white chevrons sometimes stand beside the road; very common next door too.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Green direction signs with road numbers starting with A, which South Africa never uses.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: An older style of road sign has a blue background, relatively unique here; most signs are the newer white style.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Small shacks to middle-class bungalows, some with exposed grey bricks and occasional traditional round huts.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Small random blurs cover odd parts of panoramas, especially in towns.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Coverage is limited; densest in the east and near the capital, with some unpaved rural roads.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Semi-arid shrub-covered hills between the capital and Lobatse in the southeast; most of the country is flat.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The eastern pocket north of Francistown has firm red soil, yellowing leaves and many bare withered trees.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A large mid-west region has very white sandy soil and dry vegetation; Maun shares it.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The A35 always has a power line to the west, grainy asphalt with faded markings and small tracks running beside it.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The A33 is unusually lush, with green leaves and very tall grass that grows richer further north.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The road along the southern border through Middlepits has red-tinted asphalt and an arid landscape.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A lone hill with radio antennas on the north side of Francistown; Serowe has a taller red-and-white version on a flat-topped hill.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Small winding dirt roads with scattered lush bushes and wildlife such as elephants in the far north.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Large protruding hills with exposed rock faces, on dirt roads, mark a World Heritage site.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Distinctive silos can be seen all around the town of Pandamatenga.
